candidates.explanation: Strong SSE and job lifecycle design with safe normalized contracts and transport-specific orchestration. However, capability files are scattered across application, domain, infrastructure, and jobs rather than colocated under one capability root, and the provider abstraction is described but no explicit application-owned port is placed in the tree.

The framework-neutral operation, explicit provider port, native channel contracts, failure taxonomy, and provider-safe types are coherent. The capability is dispersed across many top-level architectural folders, and the proposed Route Handler is placed under src/adapters rather than an App Router app/**/route.ts runtime surface or an explicit re-export from one.

Clearly satisfies the required Route Handler/SSE lifecycle, cancellation propagation, idle-gap timeout, post-commit failure event, report-once ownership, provider seam, and job decisions. Its main rubric shortcoming is placement: assistant behavior is distributed across domain, use-cases, adapters, infrastructure, UI, and app roots instead of one capability root.

Provides a coherent capability-rooted design with only the justified App Router and page runtime surfaces outside the module. It uses a framework-neutral generation operation and application-owned provider port, preserves SSE and job-native lifecycles, propagates abort, implements an idle rather than total timeout, changes failure representation after commit, reports unexpected failures at channel boundaries, and prevents provider details from leaking.
